newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas corn, soybean harvest ahead of schedule.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas corn, soybean harvest ahead of schedule.

text.p: Harvest of Arkansas's soybean, corn, sorghum and rice crops progressed ahead of schedule after a week of below-normal temperatures and dry weather, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its report for the week ended Sunday.

Soybeans were 23 percent harvested, even with last year's pace and slightly above a five-year average pace of 21 percent. The crop was 43 percent mature, up from 37 percent last year and a five-year average of 35 percent.
Rice was 95 percent harvested, also ahead of last year's 90 percent and the average of 87 percent. Cotton was 46 percent harvested versus 48 percent a year ago and a five-year average of 43 percent.
Corn was 99 percent harvested, up from an average 97 percent. Sorghum was 94 percent harvested.
Wheat planting also continued in several counties.
The wheat crop was 15 percent planted and seven percent emerged, versus an average emergence percentage of 7 percent and a planting average of 18 percent, the report said.
